findings.reason: §30 exists so §25's question is answerable from the service's own record, and without a verdict for a request the pass never reaches, a builder implements the pass exactly as written and the lane-filter cause remains unreadable, which is one of the two candidates §29 was written to unblock.
findings.text: §30 promises a log whose verdict list is "launched, held for allowance, held by the gate, held on its retry back-off …, held behind an earlier request, or refused", while its Why names "never considered" as one of the states that must become visible; but the pass writes a line only "for every pass whose lane has a queued pointer", and `admit_once` selects that set by `str(pointer.get("backend")) == lane` before it does anything else (reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:805-808), so a request whose recorded backend names no service the lane drains — §25's first candidate, the §24 fault class — produces a pass with no queued pointer and therefore no line, and is indistinguishable from an idle lane; the same gap swallows a pass that returns at the waiting-gate branch (queue_admission.py:795-797) before any pointer is read, even though "held by the gate" is in the enumeration

response_events.reason: valid; §30 belongs to another session and builds after §28 by its own dependency; recorded as comment c-s30-never-considered on §30 for its author to revise before §30 is dispatched

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the discard spool record this section cites exists and carries exactly `run_id`, `discarded_at`, `phase`, `node`, `pointer_path`; the §25 investigation run `r-20261018T172824230380-…` exists; `_write_discard_record`, `_stamp_failure`, `_retry_backoff_hold`, `admit_until_stopped` and `pick-timings.jsonl` all resolve, and §29's pointer-key list (`queued_at`, `session`, `backend`, `reason`, `hold` with nested `held`) matches `_queued_request_record` and the allowance dict at `dispatch_plan.py:1251`.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — §29's gate fails when the record drops the fields (its negative control) and asserts both the spool and the run-directory landing plus `discard_recorded`; §30's gate fails when the append is removed and names the retry-back-off case that the previous review found missing. Both are measurable and both declare a control.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections log under the run directory (`~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/<run>/`), which survives the run, and §30's product log sits under the crew home beside `pick-timings.jsonl` (`reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:26`); nothing lands in a scratchpad or node-local temporary path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — neither section introduces a plan label, stage name, ticket number or version tag into code; §29's page anchor `c-s28-cause-stale-admit` lives in §28, not in these units.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §30's Why names "never considered" among the states that leave no trace, and §25's own investigation listed it as a state the log must make distinguishable, but §30's verdict enumeration and its "writes nothing" rule cannot record it, so the class the previous review settled (the lane filter) stays unanswerable.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §29 carries one deliverable (the discard record keeps the admission fields) and §30 one (a per-pass verdict line), each with the bound/lifetime as a property of the same deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §30 declares `s30 → s28` for the shared `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` and the plan-section-depends-on meta carries exactly that edge; §29 writes only `reckon/crew/promotion.py`, which no other open section writes, and declares no order, so nothing is missing or mispointed.
